title: Network Programming, Scapy & Packet Analysis (PYTH_177_S1 to PYTH_177_S8)

slides.title: Packet Crafting with Scapy
slides.prompt: Scapy is a powerful Python packet manipulation tool capable of forging, sniffing, and dissecting network traffic across OSI layers.
slides.codeSnippet:
from scapy.all import IP, TCP, sr1

packet = IP(dst='1.1.1.1')/TCP(dport=80, flags='S')
response = sr1(packet)

slides.title: Layer Stacking Operator
slides.prompt: Fill in the Scapy overload operator used to stack protocol layers together (e.g., IP / TCP).

slides.title: Packet Sniffing with Filters
slides.prompt: Which function in Scapy captures network traffic matching BPF (Berkeley Packet Filter) syntax?

slides.title: Send and Receive at Layer 3
slides.prompt: Fill in the Scapy function used to send a Layer 3 packet and wait for the first answer.

slides.title: Raw Sockets Requirement
slides.prompt: Why does executing raw packet crafting scripts with Scapy require elevated administrator/root privileges?
options: Accessing raw network sockets to bypass standard kernel TCP/IP stack abstractions requires system admin rights
Scapy compiles Python code directly into Linux kernel C modules
To allow downloading external PCAP file drivers dynamically
Scapy disables network firewall settings globally across the machine
slides.correctAnswer: Accessing raw network sockets to bypass standard kernel TCP/IP stack abstractions requires system admin rights

slides.title: Reading PCAP Capture Files
slides.prompt: Fill in the Scapy function used to parse and read existing PCAP capture files into Python list objects.

slides.title: TCP SYN Stealth Scanning
slides.prompt: How does a TCP SYN scan determine if a remote port is open without completing a full 3-way handshake?
options: If the target responds with SYN-ACK, the port is open; the scanner then sends RST to terminate immediately
By sending UDP echo requests to the target port
By opening a full HTTP web socket session
By analyzing ICMP Destination Unreachable error packets
slides.correctAnswer: If the target responds with SYN-ACK, the port is open; the scanner then sends RST to terminate immediately
